new_roles.title: Operations Director
new_roles.description:
**Build Your Career. Lead With Precision.**

Nammo Perry is a center of excellence for the design, development and production of munitions and pyrotechnic products for the U.S. Department of Defense. Nammo employees working at the Florida site manufacture all types of 40mm low and high velocity ammunition; pyrotechnic marking; signaling and tactical illumination devices; battlefield effects training simulators; demolition charges; hand grenade fuzes; and other ammunition components. Additionally, they provide load, assemble, and pack (LAP) services for large caliber direct-fire ammunition.

The **Director of Operations** provides strategic and operational leadership for manufacturing, energetic material processing, maintenance, and facilities functions across the Nammo Perry facility. Reporting directly to the Site President/General Manager this position is responsible for ensuring safe, efficient, compliant, and reliable operations while supporting organizational growth production readiness and long-term business objectives.

The Director of Operations leads a multidisciplinary organization through direct-report managers responsible for Energetic Operations, Production Operations, Maintenance, and Facilities. These functions collectively support the site's manufacturing capabilities, critical infrastructure, equipment reliability, and operational continuity. The Director of Operations is expected to establish clear operational priorities, develop strong management teams, drive accountability, and foster a culture of continuous improvement grounded in Nammo’s core values of Dedication, Care, and Precision.

**Unique Benefits Designed with Care:**

* Monday - Thursday work week working 10-hour days
* Relocation assistance provided
* 401(K) with a 6% company match
* 100% Employer-Paid Employee Only Medical Plan Option
* Employer Health Saving Account Contributions
* Two week’s vacation, one-week sick pay, and nine paid holidays

**What You’ll Do: Precision in Action**

**Strategic Operations Leadership**

* Develop and execute operational strategies aligned with organizational objectives, production requirements, and long-term business growth.
* Provide leadership and accountability across manufacturing, energetic operations, maintenance, and facilities ensuring effective coordination and operational performance.
* Monitor key performance indicators related to safety, quality, delivery costs, productivity, and operational efficiency.
* Partner with site leadership to evaluate operational priorities, resource allocation, capital investments, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

**Manufacturing and Energetic Operations**

* Oversee production operations across Large Caliber Systems and Aerospace Propulsion business units ensuring safe, efficient, and compliant manufacturing activities.
* Provide strategic oversight of energetic material blending and processing operations, ensuring alignment with production requirements and established safety standards.
* Drive manufacturing performance through effective capacity planning workforce utilization production scheduling and operational discipline.
* Collaborate with engineering, quality, supply chain, and program management to support customer commitments, resolve operational challenges, and improve manufacturing capabilities.
* Ensure adequate staffing levels and resource planning to meet programmatic needs while maintaining cost initiatives.
* Establish leader standard work directives to guide day-to-day operations.

**Maintenance and Facilities Management**

* Provide strategic oversight of maintenance operations including electrical and control systems, machining, mechanical maintenance, and equipment reliability.
* Lead facilities management functions supporting site infrastructure, facilities engineering, building systems, preventative maintenance, and essential site services.
* Establish and deconflict priorities for preventative maintenance, equipment availability, infrastructure improvements, and operational continuity.
* Support capital improvements, equipment upgrades, and facility investments necessary to sustain and expand manufacturing operations.

**Safety, Quality and Regulatory Compliance**

* Champion a safety-first culture ensuring operational adherence to applicable environmental health, explosive safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Quality to maintain process discipline, product conformity, risk management, and compliance with established management systems.
* Drive accountability for identifying and addressing operational risks, safety concerns, non-conformances, and continuous improvement opportunities.

**Financial Performance and People Leadership**

* Develop and manage operational budgets, labor resources, capital expenditures, and cost improvement initiatives.
* Lead, coach, and develop direct-report managers while establishing clear expectations for performance, accountability, and organizational effectiveness.Partner with People and Culture on workforce planning, succession planning, leadership development, and employee engagement.

**What Dedicated Teammates Bring**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration or related field. Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing operations or industrial leadership.
* Minimum of 5 years of management experience including demonstrated success leading managers or multidisciplinary operational teams.
* Experience in aerospace, defense, energetic materials, chemical processing, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated ability to lead complex manufacturing operations, develop operational strategies, manage budgets, and drive performance improvements.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, industrial safety, equipment reliability, and operational excellence principles.
* Proven leadership, communication, problem solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

*Preferred Qualification:*

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Business Administration, Operations Management or related discipline.
* Direct experience in defense manufacturing, energetic material processing, ammunition production, or aerospace propulsion.
* Experience overseeing multiple operational functions including production, maintenance, facilities, and engineering support.
* Familiarity with explosive safety requirements and defense industry regulations.
* Experience with ISO 9001 and AS9100, Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or comparable operational excellence methodologies.

*Leadership Competencies*

* Aligns operational capabilities and resources with business objectives and long-term growth.
* Drives performance improvements in safety, quality, delivery cost, and reliability.
* Build strong management teams and promotes accountability, engagement, and succession readiness.
* Demonstrate sound judgment, hazard awareness, and commitment to disciplined operations,
* Build effective partnerships across departments and business units
* Leads teams through expansion, organizational growth, and evolving operational requirements.

**Our Woking Conditions and Requirements**

* This position operates in both office and industrial manufacturing environments and requires regular interaction with production areas, maintenance, operations, and facility infrastructure.
* The role may involve prolonged periods of sitting, standing, and walking, including navigating manufacturing facilities and operational work areas.
* Employees must comply with applicable safety, security, and environmental requirements including the use of required personal protective equipment (PPE) when entering designated areas.
* The position may require occasional domestic or international travel and flexibility to support operational needs outside standard business hours.
* Must be able to perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

*Our values are the fundamental principles guiding the way we do business and interact with stakeholders.*

***DEDICATION:*** *We are enthusiastic and creative, always searching for the best solutions.* 
***PRECISION:*** *We are reliable and accurate in our technology, processes and business.* 
***CARE:*** *We are inclusive and open-minded, always encouraging team spirit and cooperation.*

*Nammo and its subsidiaries provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.*

*This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.*

**\*\*Note\*\*: Due to US Export Control laws and regulations; applicants selected for employment must show proof of a U.S. Person status before employment may begin.**

new_roles.title: Supply Chain & Production Director
new_roles.description:
**Supply Chain & Production Director**

**Bil-Jax, Inc.**

**Location:** Archbold, Ohio (On-Site)

Note: Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

 

**Bil-Jax, Inc., a member of the Haulotte Group, is seeking an experienced Supply Chain & Production Director to lead manufacturing and supply chain operations at our Archbold, Ohio facility.** Reporting directly to the Vice President & General Manager, this key leadership role is responsible for manufacturing, procurement, inventory, warehousing, logistics, and Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP). The successful candidate will lead a multi-year factory modernization initiative focused on automation, operational excellence, and scalable growth while partnering with production, engineering, sourcing, and commercial teams to improve productivity, delivery performance, and profitability across the business.

 

**Key Responsibilities**

 

**Factory Modernization & Automation**

* Lead the development and execution of a long-term automation strategy that improves manufacturing efficiency, increases throughput, and reduces overall production costs.
* Manage capital investment projects from concept through implementation, including equipment selection, vendor management, installation, commissioning, and performance validation.
* Partner with Engineering and IT teams to integrate new manufacturing technologies and digital solutions that improve visibility, reporting, and operational decision-making.

 

**Production Planning & Operational Excellence**

* Optimize production scheduling and resource allocation across a complex manufacturing environment with approximately 2,000 active SKUs while maintaining high levels of quality, efficiency, and on-time delivery.
* Develop and implement processes that improve the flow of work-in-process material and eliminate bottlenecks between fabrication, welding, painting, and assembly operations.
* Lead the monthly Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process in collaboration with cross-functional leaders to align customer demand, production capacity, inventory levels, and business objectives.

 

**Supply Chain & Procurement Leadership**

* Develop sourcing strategies for steel, purchased components, and other critical materials while building strong supplier partnerships and mitigating supply chain risk.
* Establish inventory management practices that improve inventory accuracy, increase inventory turns, and maintain service levels required to support customers and production operations.
* Oversee warehousing, inbound logistics, and outbound freight activities to ensure efficient material flow and cost-effective distribution.

 

**Leadership & Organizational Development**

* Drive organizational change by leading the transition toward a more automated and technically advanced manufacturing environment while developing and upskilling existing team members.
* Provide leadership and direction to Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Production Supervisors, and other operational teams while working collaboratively with Maintenance, Safety, Shipping, and Site Leadership.
* Promote a culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement by ensuring compliance with company policies, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.

 

**Minimum Qualifications**

* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience within a manufacturing environment, including at least 5 years in a senior operations leadership role such as Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or Director of Operations.
* Demonstrated success within structural steel fabrication, sheet metal fabrication, machining, heavy equipment manufacturing, or a related industrial environment.
* Proven experience implementing manufacturing automation, robotics, or automated production cells.
* Experience leading operations within a manufacturing organization ranging from approximately $30M to $100M in annual revenue.
* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, or a related field.

 

**Preferred Skills**

* Deep understanding of metal fabrication, welding, machining, and assembly processes.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Strong financial and business acumen with experience managing operational budgets and capital expenditures.
* Experience utilizing ERP systems in a manufacturing environment, preferably Epicor.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and change management skills.

new_roles.title: Director of Millwork Production
new_roles.description:
About the Position

We are an established architectural woodwork and custom millwork company based in Coconut Creek, Florida, seeking an experienced Production Manager / Shop Foreman to lead the day-to-day operations of our millwork shop.

This is a hands-on leadership position for someone with strong experience in architectural millwork, custom cabinetry, woodworking, and shop production.

You will be responsible for keeping production organized and moving—from approved drawings and materials through fabrication, assembly, quality control, and preparation for delivery and installation.

We are looking for someone who can lead people, organize workflow, maintain quality, solve production problems, and take ownership of the shop floor.

Key Responsibilities

* Manage daily architectural millwork and cabinetry production
* Schedule and prioritize jobs based on project deadlines and installation requirements
* Assign work to shop employees and monitor production progress
* Read and interpret architectural drawings, shop drawings, elevations, details, and specifications
* Review drawings and materials before fabrication to identify missing information or potential production issues
* Coordinate closely with Project Managers regarding priorities, changes, field conditions, and project requirements
* Ensure materials, hardware, and components are available when required
* Oversee cutting, machining, fabrication, assembly, and preparation for delivery
* Maintain quality control throughout the production process
* Inspect completed work for dimensions, workmanship, drawings, specifications, and company standards
* Identify and resolve production problems quickly
* Coordinate with installation teams to ensure fabricated components are properly prepared for the field
* Track production schedules and communicate potential delays before they become critical
* Train, supervise, and hold shop personnel accountable for quality, productivity, and workmanship
* Maintain an organized, clean, and safe shop
* Improve shop workflow, organization, efficiency, and production processes
* Ensure completed millwork is properly labeled, protected, packaged, and ready for delivery
* Help maintain machinery, tools, equipment, and other shop resources
* Enforce company safety procedures and proper equipment use

Required Qualifications

* 5+ years of relevant experience in architectural millwork, custom cabinetry, woodworking, or a closely related trade
* Previous experience as a Shop Foreman, Production Manager, Millwork Foreman, Lead Carpenter, or similar leadership position
* Strong understanding of architectural millwork and custom fabrication
* Ability to read and interpret architectural plans and shop drawings
* Strong knowledge of woodworking materials, hardware, fabrication methods, and construction techniques
* Experience supervising and directing shop or production employees
* Strong understanding of quality control and professional millwork craftsmanship
* Ability to schedule and prioritize multiple projects and deadlines
* Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
* Ability to communicate effectively with Project Managers, installers, vendors, and shop employees
* Ability to take ownership of shop operations and work independently
* Hands-on leadership style and willingness to work directly on the shop floor when needed

Preferred Experience

Experience with any of the following is a plus:

* CNC machinery and CNC-based production
* Cabinet manufacturing
* Architectural woodwork
* High-end commercial or residential millwork
* Laminates, veneers, solid wood, and specialty materials
* Millwork hardware and specialty components
* Finishing and coordination with finishing vendors
* Cabinet Vision, AutoCAD, or similar software
* Production scheduling and job tracking systems
* Commercial construction and field installation coordination

What We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who can run the shop—not simply supervise it.

The right person will know what is in production, what needs to be produced next, where potential problems exist, and what needs to happen to keep projects on schedule.

You should be comfortable leading employees while remaining actively involved on the shop floor.

Success in this position means maintaining an organized, productive shop that consistently produces high-quality millwork on schedule while minimizing mistakes, rework, and delays.

Compensation & Opportunity

* $80,000–$120,000 per year, depending on experience
* Bonus eligible
* Full-time position
* Stable, established architectural millwork company
* Opportunity for growth and increased responsibility
* Significant responsibility for shop operations and production
* Work on high-quality custom architectural millwork projects throughout South Florida

How to Apply

Please submit your resume through Indeed.

Candidates with direct architectural millwork or custom cabinetry experience should clearly identify that experience on their resume, including previous shop leadership responsibilities and the types of products or projects they have managed.

Pay: $95,000.00 - $150,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Relocation assistance

Work Location: In person

new_roles.title: Director, Filling & Assembly
new_roles.description:
At Revlon, we create beauty innovations for everyone that inspire confidence and ignite joy every day.

Breaking beauty boundaries is in our company's DNA. Since its game-changing launch of the first opaque nail enamel in 1932 (and later, the first long-wear foundation), Revlon has provided consumers with high-quality product innovation, performance, and sophisticated glamour. Elizabeth Arden made waves as a woman-led beauty company in the 1920s. In 1931, Almay became the original hypoallergenic, fragrance-free beauty brand.

Today, Revlon resiliently continues its legacy as a leading global beauty company. Our diverse portfolio—which consists of some of the world's most iconic brands and product offerings in color cosmetics, skincare, hair color & care, personal care, and fragrances—is sold around the world through prestige, professional, mass, and direct-to-consumer retail channels. These brands include Revlon, Revlon Professional, Elizabeth Arden, Almay, American Crew, CND, Cutex, Mitchum, Sinful Colors, Creme of Nature, Christina Aguilera, John Varvatos, Juicy Couture, Ed Hardy and more.

We honor our heritage, embrace change, and applaud diversity. We champion our employees and celebrate our consumers.

We are Revlon, together, transforming beauty.

**This role is an Onsite Role:** This role requires full-time presence at our Oxford, NC office.

**Overview:**

* Responsible for the safe and efficient operation of the Oxford Filling and Assembly operation – may include multiple cost centers (or all). Specific responsibilities include Ensuring that the workplace is safe, and employees work in a safe manner; Provide that all GMP requirements and regulations are complied with; Ensuring that all people issues and developmental needs are met; monitoring production requirements such that all customer needs are met on a timely basis; Responsible for all financial results of the operation.
* Act as a backup to the Vice President of Manufacturing (as needed) and the Oxford site General Manager (as needed). Be aware of any major issues/action underway in other cost centers / production areas in order to fill in as needed.

**Responsibilities:**

* **Safety:** Ensure that a safe workplace is maintained at all times. Provide resources necessary to be proactive towards addressing issues in the workplace. Comply with all OSHA & Revlon guidelines and procedures. Assist Safety Director as needed with task forces, projects and teams. Measures: Safety incident rate; OSHA & Workmen's comp rates; Revlon Safety Index.
* **People:** Strive to make the Oxford site a great place to work by: proactively developing people (cross training, class work and challenges); Addressing all issues, concerns and disciplinary actions promptly and effectively; contributing to site efforts to address issues and concerns. Measures: GPTW survey results; Developmental activity; providing challenges & changes to drive the organization forward.
* **GMP / Regulatory:** Ensure that all Revlon & Governmental Good Manufacturing Practices are complied with. Provide resources necessary to address any issues before the operation is adversely affected. Work with the site Quality Director (and others – as needed) to implement any new requirements due to new products or new regulations. Provide / facilitate training as needed. Ensure that all appropriate records are accurate and maintained within guidelines. Measures: First pass yields, rejection rates (domestic and international); GMP audit scores.
* **Customer Service:** Ensure that all Customer requirements (domestic, international & special markets) are met per company objectives (Regular business forecast & Promotional commitments). Evaluate production needs on a forward basis to ensure that needed equipment and people resources are available to meet the customer's needs. Measures: Schedule adherence; % Dollars shipped vs. ordered (CSL); performance to promotional ship on time commitments.
* **Financial:** Responsible for all financial aspects of the Filling and Assembly operation: Control of Labor – Direct (productive effort); Indirect (support effort); Nonstandard (Rework & First pass yield issues); Material – performance to established standards & minimization of waste; Overhead – effective utilization of management staff, supplies and ancillary equipment; Capital – effective, proactive utilization of installed equipment base, addressing capacity and new product needs with adequate lead time to meet customer's needs. Support and facilitate site cost reduction objectives. Measures: Labor – Direct efficiency, indirect % to earned, nonstandard % to earned; Material – MUV; Overhead – performance to budget & tasks.
* + Overhead – Supplies, executive staff, support labor – Up to $14 Million annually
 + Material – Value of material moved through the filling and assembly operation - $250 Million annually
 + Labor – Direct Labor managed in the filling and assembly operation - $30 Million annually

**Responsible for establishing processes to:**

* Ensure that all employees in the operation have defined job duties and expectations and are managed according to those duties – and that timely corrective action takes place when needed.
* Ensure that reasonable schedules are formulated, meeting customer's needs and equipment capability. Interface with appropriate departments as needed to affect change.
* Ensure that all equipment is operational and performs within expected tolerances.
* Ensure that all Revlon and governmental policies, guidelines, rules and procedures are followed and adhered to.
* Interface with all other sites functional areas as needed (HR, Quality, Distribution, Finance, etc.)

**Qualifications:**

* Extensive knowledge of production equipment, especially safe operating techniques, product capabilities and trouble-shooting methods
* Knowledge of planning / scheduling forecasting processes and systems
* Knowledge and experience with operations in an FDA – GMP environment
* Significant communication skills – verbal and written
* High level ability to analyze situations, and ability to facilitate cross functional teams
* Demonstrated success in people development and driving an organization forward
* Basic computer skills including Excel, Word, and use of MRP systems
* Prefer a 4-year degree in an engineering discipline, but other areas of study will be considered with appropriate and relevant experience
* Minimum 15 years of experience required
* Ability to make decisions
* Ability to effectively set and enforce company policy affecting up to 2,500 employees – communicate changes and issues to said group
* Significant operating knowledge of the Cosmetic industry – products, equipment and business practices
* Knowledge of Customer / Supplier relationships and how to best manage those to get results

Shift hours: 8:00am - 5:00pm

#LI-JL1

**Revlon is unable to sponsor or transfer employment visas for this role; candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future visa support.**

The base pay range for this position is $125,000 - $165,000 / year; however base pay offered may vary depending on skills, experience, job-related knowledge, and geographic location. Certain positions may also be eligible for short-term incentives as part of total compensation.

Employees (and their families) are eligible for medical, dental, and vision benefits. Employees are covered by the company-paid basic life insurance policy and company-paid short-term disability insurance (the benefit commences upon hire and allows for a portion of base salary for up to 26 weeks if you are disabled). Other benefits offered to employees include but are not limited to the following: long-term disability, supplemental life insurances, flexible spending accounts, critical illness insurance, group legal, identity theft protection, etc. Employees are also able to enroll in our 401k Retirement Savings Plan.

Employees will also receive 4 weeks of vacation, pro-rated based on date of hire for the 1st year of employment and twelve paid holidays throughout the calendar year. Vacation will depend on role.

Applicant Privacy Notice

Privacy policy – Revlon

new_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

**Job Title** 
Plant Manager (Angleton, TX)

**Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World**

Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a diversity of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers.

**The Impact You’ll Make in this Role** 
As a Plant Senior Manager you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative and diverse people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:

 

* EHS stewardship and compliance to ensure operational Environmental, Health, and Safety compliance and accountability. EHS active visible leadership, ownership, and involvement within all operations.
* Driving strategic planning and budgeting to drive sustainable improvements in factory cost through application of continuous improvement, entitlement thinking, yield improvement, and plant productivity.
* Managing supply chain execution and inventory management to ensure appropriate customer value stream performance through responsiveness, delivery performance, LTA, capacity management, supplier management, and appropriate inventory management including working and non-working inventory.
* Accelerating value creation for our customers through responsive end-to-end supply chain performance and prompt resolution to customer inquiries
* Developing manufacturing strategies for a high-performance workforce, capital equipment planning, technology advancement, and employee and leadership development.
* Championing inclusive programs that create a great place to work for all our employees

**Your Skills and Expertise** 
To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:

 

* Bachelor's degree or higher (completed and verified prior to start) from an accredited institution
* Four (4) years of supervisory and/or management experience in a private, public, government or military environment
* Five (5) years of manufacturing experience in a private, public, government or military environment

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:

 

* Experience managing and/or supervising direct reports
* Demonstrated strong leadership ability and history of leading high-performance teams
* Demonstrated understanding of principle-based leadership and behaviors
* Bachelor’s degree or higher in an engineering discipline
* Experience in leading strategic and organizational development, operational excellence, lean implementation, financial accounting
* Effective communication skills

**Work location:**

* **Angleton, T**X

**Travel: May include up to 10%** **domestic/international**

**Relocation Assistance: May be authorized**

**Must be legally authorized to work in country of employment without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status).**

*Responsibilities of this position may include direct and/or indirect physical or logical access to information, systems, technologies subjected to the* *regulations/compliance* *with U.S. Export Control Laws.*

*U.S. Export Control laws and U.S. Government Department of Defense contracts and sub-contracts impose certain restrictions on companies and their ability to share export-controlled and other technology and services with certain "non-U.S. persons" (persons who are not U.S. citizens or nationals, lawful permanent residents of the U.S., refugees, "Temporary Residents" (granted Amnesty or Special Agricultural Worker provisions), or persons granted asylum.*

*The questions asked in this application are intended to assess this and will be used for evaluation purposes only. Failure to provide the necessary information in this regard will result in our inability to consider you further for this particular position.*

**Supporting Your Well-being**

3M offers many programs to help you live your best life – both physically and financially. To ensure competitive pay and benefits, 3M regularly benchmarks with other companies that are comparable in size and scope.

For assistance with searching through our current job openings or for more information about all things 3M, visit Max, our virtual recruiting assistant on 3M.com/careers.

new_roles.description:
Linde Advanced Material Technologies Inc.

**Plant Manager**

Ellisville, MS, United States | req34514

**What you will enjoy doing\***

* Lead the Ellisville manufacturing operation with full accountability for Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC), while ensuring customer commitments and business objectives are consistently achieved
* Build and develop a high-performing leadership team by setting clear expectations, coaching managers and supervisors, strengthening accountability, and developing organizational capability and succession
* You will drive the PGT Lean Operating System through daily management, leader standard work, visual management, structured problem solving, standard work, and continuous improvement
* Be a visible leader on the shop floor, working with teams at the source to identify problems, remove barriers, strengthen process discipline, and ensure corrective actions address root causes and are sustained
* Improve operational performance and reliability by strengthening equipment performance, first-pass yield, flow, WIP, productivity, capacity, and on-time delivery while maintaining uncompromising safety and quality standards
* Develop and execute the site strategy, aligning workforce, training, equipment, materials, capital, and capacity with customer demand, growth priorities, and long-term business requirements
* Own the financial performance of the facility, including budgets, labor efficiency, overtime, productivity, cost improvement, operational spending, and capital priorities
* Also, you will lead cross-functionally and create a strong site culture, partnering with Operations, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Maintenance, EHS, Human Resources, and Finance while fostering respect, transparency, employee engagement, urgency, and continuous improvement

**What makes you great**

* You have a Bachelor’s degree with ten (10) or more years of related manufacturing experience, a Master’s degree with eight (8) or more years, a PhD with five (5) or more years, or sixteen (16) or more years of directly related manufacturing experience
* Further you have significant manufacturing leadership experience with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, people, and operational results
* You have successfully led leaders, including managers and frontline supervisors, and know how to build capability rather than becoming the organization’s primary problem solver
* You have demonstrated experience applying Lean principles, daily management, standard work, and structured problem solving to deliver measurable operational improvement
* And you bring strong financial and business acumen, with experience managing budgets, labor, productivity, operating costs, and capital priorities
* Experience in aerospace, coatings, special processes, precision manufacturing, or another highly regulated manufacturing environment is strongly preferred
* You are comfortable leading change in a complex manufacturing environment and can move effectively between strategy, data, the shop floor, and customer and business priorities
* Most importantly, you lead with humility, accountability, transparency, respect for people, and a bias for action, while developing others and creating sustainable systems for success

**Why you will love working with us**

Linde is a leading global industrial gases and engineering company with 2025 sales of $34 billion. We live our mission of making our world more productive every day by providing high-quality solutions, technologies and services which are making our customers more successful and helping to sustain, decarbonize and protect our planet.
 
 
Linde serves a variety of end markets such as chemicals & energy, food & beverage, electronics, healthcare, manufacturing, metals and mining. Linde’s industrial gases and technologies are used in countless applications, enabling space exploration and launch technologies, delivering ultra-high-purity and specialty gases for semiconductor manufacturing, providing life-saving medical oxygen and enabling clean hydrogen production and carbon capture to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Linde also delivers state-of-the-art gas processing solutions to support customer growth, efficiency improvements and emissions reductions.

**What we offer you!**

At Linde, the sky is not the limit. If you’re looking to build a career where your work reaches beyond your job description and betters the people with whom you work, the communities we serve, and the world in which we all live, at Linde, your opportunities are limitless. Be Linde. Be Limitless. 
 
Linde offers competitive compensation and an outstanding benefits package. Enjoy access to health, dental, disability, and life insurance, paid holidays and vacation, 401(k) matching, pension benefits, an employee discount program, and opportunities for educational and professional growth. Additional compensation may vary depending on the position and organizational level. Build your future with us while making an impact every day!

**Have we inspired you? Let´s talk about it**

We are looking forward to receiving your complete application.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other reason prohibited by applicable law. 
 
Linde Advanced Material Technologies Inc. abides by applicable export control laws including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) in accordance with the company's export control procedures. As such, persons considered for this position must be either a U.S. Citizen, Permanent Resident (green card holder) or otherwise classifiable as a U.S. person under relevant regulations. 
 
Linde Advanced Material Technologies Inc. acts responsibly towards its shareholders, business partners, employees, society and the environment in every one of its business areas, regions and locations across the globe. The company is committed to technologies and products that unite the goals of customer value and sustainable development. 
 

* The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of employees assigned to this position. Therefore employees assigned may be required to perform additional job tasks required by the manager.

new_roles.title: Manufacturing Plant Manager - CT
new_roles.description:
**Job Summary:**

The Plant Manager is responsible for leading all day-to-day manufacturing operations at the site, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality production. This role owns execution of production, cost, delivery, and safety performance, while aligning with corporate standards across quality, engineering, supply chain, and HR. The Plant Manager drives operational discipline, team performance, and continuous improvement to deliver consistent, predictable results.

 

**Company Overview:**

PTA Plastics, an employee-owned and innovative leader in the plastic injection molding, contract manufacturing and tool-building industry, is looking for a Plant Manager to join our dynamic team.

At PTA Plastics, we’re more than just a manufacturer; we partner with Fortune 500 OEMs in the medical device, defense, homeland security, and technology sectors, constantly pushing the boundaries of product development and manufacturing excellence. As an employee-owned company, every team member has a stake in our success, creating a collaborative and entrepreneurial environment where innovation thrives.

**Pay:** $150,000 - $190,000 annually

 

**Essential Duties/Responsibilities:**

**Site P&L Performance**

* Own site-level financial performance

* Deliver budgeted profitability, labor efficiency, and cost targets

* Control overtime, scrap, and operating expenses

 

**Production & Operational Execution**

* Lead all day-to-day plant operations

* Ensure schedule attainment and on-time delivery

* Drive production efficiency, uptime, and throughput

* Remove operational roadblocks quickly

* Lead and resolve customer escalations at the plant level

 

**Safety & Compliance**

* Own plant safety performance

* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental, and company standards

* Drive a proactive, behavior-based safety culture

 

**People Leadership & Culture**

* Lead and develop plant leadership team and floor personnel

* Drive accountability, performance management, and clear expectations

* Build a high-performance, no-excuses culture

 

**Execution of Corporate Quality Standards**

* Ensure adherence to corporate Quality Management System (QMS)

* Support and enforce corrective actions

* Hold production teams accountable for quality at the source

 

**Execution of Corporate Engineering Standards**

* Maintain schedule discipline and production alignment with planning

* Resolve plant-level material and supply issues

* Support inventory control and flow

 

**Cross Functional Alignment**

* Corporate Quality

* Corporate Engineering

* Corporate Supply Chain

* Corporate HR

 

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead Lean and continuous improvement initiatives

* Reduce scrap, downtime, and inefficiencies

* Improve labor utilization and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)

 

**Qualifications & Requirements:**

#### **Education & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations Management, Business, or a related field required (or equivalent combination of education and experience)
* 7–10+ years of manufacturing experience, preferably in injection molding or a similar high-volume, process-driven environment
* 3–5+ years of leadership experience managing production teams and plant operations
* Proven track record of delivering results in:
 + Production output and schedule attainment
 + Cost control and labor efficiency
 + Safety and quality performance
* Experience leading in a metrics-driven environment (OEE, scrap, uptime, etc.)
* Hands-on experience with Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and waste reduction initiatives
* Experience working within structured corporate environments with cross-functional support (Quality, Engineering, Supply Chain, HR)
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems and production planning processes

#### **Technical & Industry Knowledge**

* Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, including production processes, workflow optimization, and plant performance metrics (OEE, uptime, scrap, labor efficiency)

* Working knowledge of injection molding processes, materials, tooling, and secondary operations (or similar high-volume manufacturing processes)

* Understanding of maintenance and reliability principles, including preventive maintenance and equipment uptime optimization

* Experience with Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and waste reduction methodologies (5S, Kaizen, standard work, etc.)

* Knowledge of quality systems and practices, including root cause analysis, corrective actions, and adherence to QMS standards (ISO or similar)

* Familiarity with production scheduling, capacity planning, and inventory flow within an ERP/MRP environment

* Understanding of workplace safety standards and regulatory compliance (OSHA, environmental requirements)

* Ability to interpret and act on operational data to drive performance improvements

 

**Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to stand, walk, and move around the production floor for extended periods.
* Capable of lifting and carrying heavy objects weighing up to 50 pounds.
* Manual dexterity and hand-eye coordination for handling small tools, machine components, and molds.
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and adapt to changing priorities.
* Comfortable wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety glasses, gloves, and ear protection.
* Occasional bending, kneeling, and reaching to access equipment and perform maintenance tasks.
* Good vision and color perception for inspecting parts and identifying any defects or abnormalities.
* Ability to work in temperature-controlled environments and withstand exposure to noise levels associated with manufacturing machinery.
* Ability to receive, comprehend and utilize required training from OSHA and Company including but not limited to the following:
* Hazard Communication
* Lock Out/Tag Out

 

**ITAR Requirements:** To conform to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(3), applicants for employment at PTA Plastics must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawfully admitted for permanent residence into the U.S. (i.e., current green card holder), or lawfully admitted as a refugee or granted asylum under 8 U.S.C. § 1157-1158.

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity & ADA Compliance Statement****:**

PTA Plastics is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all individuals, including those with disabilities. As part of this commitment, PTA Plastics complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)andConnecticut’s Fair Employment Practices Act (CFEPA)**,** which prohibit discrimination against individuals with disabilities in hiring, job assignments, promotions, compensation, benefits, training, and other aspects of employment.

 

If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or interview process or to perform the essential functions of this position, please contact HR@ptaplastics.com. Reasonable accommodations will be provided in accordance with applicable laws to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential job duties.

 

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Employees may be required to perform other duties as assigned.

**Job Summary:**

The Plant Manager is responsible for leading all day-to-day manufacturing operations at the site, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality production. This role owns execution of production, cost, delivery, and safety performance, while aligning with corporate standards across quality, engineering, supply chain, and HR. The Plant Manager drives operational discipline, team performance, and continuous improvement to deliver consistent, predictable results.

 

**Company Overview:**

PTA Plastics, an employee-owned and innovative leader in the plastic injection molding, contract manufacturing and tool-building industry, is looking for a Plant Manager to join our dynamic team.

At PTA Plastics, we’re more than just a manufacturer; we partner with Fortune 500 OEMs in the medical device, defense, homeland security, and technology sectors, constantly pushing the boundaries of product development and manufacturing excellence. As an employee-owned company, every team member has a stake in our success, creating a collaborative and entrepreneurial environment where innovation thrives.

**Pay:** $150,000 - $190,000 annually

 

**Essential Duties/Responsibilities:**

**Site P&L Performance**

* Own site-level financial performance

* Deliver budgeted profitability, labor efficiency, and cost targets

* Control overtime, scrap, and operating expenses

 

**Production & Operational Execution**

* Lead all day-to-day plant operations

* Ensure schedule attainment and on-time delivery

* Drive production efficiency, uptime, and throughput

* Remove operational roadblocks quickly

* Lead and resolve customer escalations at the plant level

 

**Safety & Compliance**

* Own plant safety performance

* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental, and company standards

* Drive a proactive, behavior-based safety culture

 

**People Leadership & Culture**

* Lead and develop plant leadership team and floor personnel

* Drive accountability, performance management, and clear expectations

* Build a high-performance, no-excuses culture

 

**Execution of Corporate Quality Standards**

* Ensure adherence to corporate Quality Management System (QMS)

* Support and enforce corrective actions

* Hold production teams accountable for quality at the source

 

**Execution of Corporate Engineering Standards**

* Maintain schedule discipline and production alignment with planning

* Resolve plant-level material and supply issues

* Support inventory control and flow

 

**Cross Functional Alignment**

* Corporate Quality

* Corporate Engineering

* Corporate Supply Chain

* Corporate HR

 

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead Lean and continuous improvement initiatives

* Reduce scrap, downtime, and inefficiencies

* Improve labor utilization and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)

#### **Education & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations Management, Business, or a related field required (or equivalent combination of education and experience)
* 7–10+ years of manufacturing experience, preferably in injection molding or a similar high-volume, process-driven environment
* 3–5+ years of leadership experience managing production teams and plant operations
* Proven track record of delivering results in:
 + Production output and schedule attainment
 + Cost control and labor efficiency
 + Safety and quality performance
* Experience leading in a metrics-driven environment (OEE, scrap, uptime, etc.)
* Hands-on experience with Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and waste reduction initiatives
* Experience working within structured corporate environments with cross-functional support (Quality, Engineering, Supply Chain, HR)
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems and production planning processes

* Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, including production processes, workflow optimization, and plant performance metrics (OEE, uptime, scrap, labor efficiency)

* Working knowledge of injection molding processes, materials, tooling, and secondary operations (or similar high-volume manufacturing processes)

* Understanding of maintenance and reliability principles, including preventive maintenance and equipment uptime optimization

* Experience with Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and waste reduction methodologies (5S, Kaizen, standard work, etc.)

* Ability to interpret and act on operational data to drive performance improvements

new_roles.title: Director of Quality
new_roles.description:
**Quality Director**

**Aerospace Manufacturing | Senior Leadership Team**

**About Columbia Manufacturing**

Columbia Manufacturing, a member of Collective Manufacturing Group, produces complex fabricated components and assemblies for leading aerospace and power generation engine programs. We are committed to delivering safe, reliable, and compliant products while fostering a culture built on integrity, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

As we continue to grow, we are seeking a Quality Director who will strengthen our quality culture, develop our people, and help ensure we remain a trusted partner to our customers.

**Position Summary**

The Quality Director is a member of the senior leadership team responsible for ensuring Columbia Manufacturing consistently delivers products that meet customer, regulatory, and internal quality requirements.

This role goes beyond compliance. We are seeking a leader who combines sound judgment, ethical decision-making, objective interpretation of requirements, and strong cross-functional leadership. The successful candidate will guide the organization through customer requirements, industry standards, and business challenges while ensuring quality and integrity remain at the center of every decision. We believe strong teams produce strong results, and cultural fit is as important as technical expertise.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative leader who earns trust, develops people, and works effectively with Production, Engineering, Supply Chain, and customers. We value practical experience as highly as formal education and welcome candidates who have built their careers through hands-on manufacturing and quality leadership roles.

**What You’ll Do**

**Lead the Quality Management System**

* Maintain and continuously improve the Quality Management System.
* Ensure compliance with customer, regulatory, and aerospace requirements.
* Promote quality ownership and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

**Guide Quality Decisions**

* Interpret customer specifications, drawings, contractual requirements, and industry standards.
* Provide guidance when requirements are unclear, conflicting, or open to interpretation.
* Lead investigations, corrective actions, and nonconformance resolution using sound judgment and risk-based decision making.

**Partner with Customers and Regulatory Bodies**

* Serve as the primary quality representative to customers, auditors, and regulatory agencies.
* Build trusted relationships and lead internal, customer, and third-party audits.

**Develop People and Culture**

* Lead, mentor, and develop the Quality team.
* Build a high-performing organization through coaching, accountability, and succession planning.
* Foster collaboration and an environment where employees are comfortable raising concerns.
* Promote a culture where doing the right thing is always more important than meeting a schedule.

**Contribute to Business Success**

* Partner with Operations and Leadership to improve performance, reduce risk, strengthen organizational alignment, and support growth.
* Balance customer expectations, business priorities, and compliance requirements without compromising quality standards.
* Exercise independent quality authority and be willing to stop production or shipment when requirements have not been met.

**What We’re Looking For**

We recognize that great leaders come from many backgrounds. Candidates may have developed through engineering, manufacturing, inspection, quality systems, operations, military service, trade programs, or traditional degree pathways. Equivalent combinations of education, military training, trade experience, and hands-on manufacturing or quality leadership experience will be fully considered.

We are less concerned with how you gained your experience and more interested in your ability to lead people, interpret requirements, make sound decisions, and uphold quality standards under pressure.

Successful candidates will typically possess:

* Experience leading quality functions within aerospace, manufacturing, or other highly regulated industries.
* Strong understanding of quality systems, customer requirements, and specification interpretation.
* Demonstrated ethical leadership, sound decision-making, and the ability to uphold standards under pressure.
* Proven success leading teams and collaborating across departments.
* Strong communication skills and experience working with customers, auditors, and senior leadership.
* Continuous improvement mindset and practical problem-solving ability.

**Preferred Experience**

* Familiarity with aerospace quality standards such as AS9100, AS9110, AS13100, NADCAP, or customer-specific requirements.
* Experience supporting OEM customers such as GE Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, or similar organizations.
* Quality certifications or advanced education are valued but not required.

**Why This Role Matters**

The Quality Director plays a critical role in protecting our customers, our employees, and our reputation. This leader helps ensure that every product we build meets requirements and that every decision we make reflects our commitment to integrity, accountability, and continuous improvement.

**If you are a leader who values ethics, teamwork, sound judgment, and building strong people and processes, we encourage you to apply.**

new_roles.title: SR. Manager Human Resources, Manufacturing (People & Culture)
new_roles.description:
**Job Description Summary:**

At The Coca-Cola Company, our people and culture are essential to how we create value, grow our business, and make a difference every day. We are looking for a **Senior Manager, Human Resources-People & Culture (Manufacturing)** who will bring strong business partnership, sound judgment, and hands-on People & Culture leadership to two manufacturing locations supporting both union and non-union associates.

 

This role is the Primary **People & Culture Leader and** visible face of **Human Resources at the plant** , serving as a trusted partner to plant leadership and an accessible resource for associates. The Senior Manager will report directly to the Plant Manager, with a dotted-line relationship to the Director, People & Culture, helping ensure strong alignment between plant priorities and broader People & Culture strategies, standards, and practices.

 

Success requires someone who can move comfortably between the plant floor and leadership discussions. You will listen to associates, coach leaders, navigate complex employee and labor relations matters, use workforce insights to inform decisions, develop talent, and translate business priorities into practical people solutions. The ideal candidate brings manufacturing Human Resources experience, labor relations capability, strong business acumen, a commitment to inclusion, and the ability to build credibility and trusted relationships at every level of the organization.

 

**Key Responsibilities and Position-Related Functions**
-------------------------------------------------------

* Serve as the senior on-site People & Culture partner for two manufacturing locations, providing hands-on leadership and support across union and non-union associate populations.
* Partner directly with the Plant Manager and plant leadership teams to translate operational and business priorities into actionable workforce, talent, culture, and organizational initiatives.
* Serve as the primary, visible People & Culture resource for associates, creating an approachable and trusted presence across shifts and levels of the organization.
* Coach and advise plant leaders on organizational effectiveness, leadership capability, performance management, accountability, employee development, workforce decisions, and people-related business challenges.
* Lead and support employee relations matters with objectivity, consistency, confidentiality, sound judgment, and appropriate partnership with the Director, People & Culture and other subject-matter experts.
* Support labor relations within the unionized location, including interpretation and consistent application of the collective bargaining agreement, issue resolution, grievance processes, and development of productive labor-management relationships.
* Partner with leaders to promote a positive, inclusive, safe, and respectful workplace where associates can contribute, grow, and thrive.
* Lead workforce planning discussions, using workforce data and operational insights to identify talent needs, retention risks, organizational opportunities, and appropriate actions.
* Strengthen leader capability in performance management, associate engagement, development conversations, conflict resolution, and consistent application of People & Culture practices.
* Partner with leaders on talent reviews, succession planning, career development, critical-role planning, and development opportunities that build plant capability.

* Provide guidance to associates and leaders on pay, benefits, leave, workplace policies, Human Resources programs, systems, and processes, engaging appropriate partners when specialized expertise is required.
* Analyze turnover, attendance, staffing, engagement, workforce demographics, and other people data to identify trends and translate insights into practical recommendations for plant leadership.

* 7+ years of progressive Human Resources experience, with meaningful experience supporting manufacturing, supply chain, distribution, or another complex operational environment.

* Experience serving as a trusted Human Resources partner to senior operational leaders and translating business priorities into effective people solutions.
* Strong employee relations capability, including experience evaluating complex workplace situations, conducting or supporting investigations, resolving conflict, managing risk, and determining when escalation or specialist partnership is appropriate.

* Experience supporting hourly and salaried populations and building credibility with associates and leaders across multiple organizational levels and work schedules.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager Quality and Safety
new_roles.description:
Site: Newton-Wellesley Hospital

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.

**Job Summary**

The Sr. Manager in this role will oversee the execution of MGB strategy, processes, and infrastructure for the domains of safety, risk and PFR. This role oversees a team of safety, risk, and PFR specialists to support the implementation of standardization of best practices and a system strategy. This role will collaborate with site leadership to execute long and short-term goals for Risk Management, Patient Safety programs, and Patient and Family Relations. 
 
Does this position require Patient Care? 
No 
 
Essential Functions 

* Support the build out of safety/risk/PFR infrastructure, ensuring standardization in training, processes, and safety responses that are in line with MGB.

 

* Executes the MGB safety plans including those around event analysis, safety event reporting/management/mitigation.

 

* Implement the standardized risk management strategy, policies, and procedures, ensuring that risk management activities both align to and augment our approach to patient safety.

 

* Implement the system-wide safety event reporting system.

 

* Support as needed for system wide safety events such as recalls, shortages, and other events that impact safety.

 

* Understand data provided by the system team and use knowledge of local practices to identify areas of opportunity for improvement of patient safety as well as communicate to the system areas that are at risk.

 

* Execute the MGB quality and clinical compliance strategy within local site ensuring adherence to MGB standardized processes around quality measurement, strategy, prioritized areas, and performance improvement while also providing critical feedback about issues and needs that are arising within local site.

 

* Liase as needed with local site Risk/Safety/PFR leader to create prospective solutions and performance improvement as a result of safety events. Partner with safety team as needed prospectively to create performance improvement in pursuit of harm avoidance.

 

* Senior local site manager responsible for Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement QAPI planning and documentation, and updates as needed for board quality committee/patient care assessment committee.

 

* Serve as the senior local site administrative manager covering compliance activities at local site, ensuring adherence to local site standardized processes around tracer activity, site level preparedness activities, and measuring/monitoring compliance.

 

* Understand data provided by the system team and use knowledge of local practices and culture to identify areas of opportunity for improvement as well as communicate to the system areas which are at risk.

 

* Provides strong bi-directional communication between the system and the site, with accountability for distribution of organization communication (including pertinent data and analytics) from MGB to local site and vice versa.

**Qualifications**

Education Bachelor's Degree Related Field of Study required or Bachelor's Degree Patient Safety Leadership required and Master's Degree Nursing preferred Can this role accept experience in lieu of a degree? No Licenses and Credentials Experience Safety, Risk Management, and patient family relations. 3-5 years required and Leading process improvement and initiatives and managing teams. 3-5 years required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities - Support the build out of safety/risk/PFR infrastructure, ensuring standardization in training, processes, and safety responses that are in line with MGB. - Executes the MGB safety plans including those around event analysis, safety event reporting/management/mitigation. - Implement the standardized risk management strategy, policies, and procedures, ensuring that risk management activities both align to and augment our approach to patient safety. - Implement the system-wide safety event reporting system. - Support as needed for system wide safety events such as recalls, shortages, and other events that impact safety. - Understand data provided by the system team and use knowledge of local practices to identify areas of opportunity for improvement of patient safety as well as communicate to the system areas that are at risk.

**Additional Job Details (if applicable)**

**Remote Type**

Hybrid

**Work Location**

2014 Washington Street

**Scheduled Weekly Hours**

40

**Employee Type**

Regular

**Work Shift**

Day (United States of America)

**Pay Range**

$99,465.60 - $144,643.20/Annual

**Grade**

8 
At Mass General Brigham, we believe in recognizing and rewarding the unique value each team member brings to our organization. Our approach to determining base pay is comprehensive, and any offer extended will take into account your skills, relevant experience if applicable, education, certifications and other essential factors. The base pay information provided offers an estimate based on the minimum job qualifications; however, it does not encompass all elements contributing to your total compensation package. In addition to competitive base pay, we offer comprehensive benefits, career advancement opportunities, differentials, premiums and bonuses as applicable and recognition programs designed to celebrate your contributions and support your professional growth. We invite you to apply, and our Talent Acquisition team will provide an overview of your potential compensation and benefits package.

**EEO Statement:**

4100 Newton-Wellesley Hospital is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religious creed, national origin, sex, age, gender identity, disability, sexual orientation, military service, genetic information, and/or other status protected under law. We will ensure that all individuals with a disability are provided a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. To ensure reasonable accommodation for individuals protected by Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Vietnam Veteran’s Readjustment Act of 1974, and Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, applicants who require accommodation in the job application process may contact Human Resources at (857)-282-7642.

**Mass General Brigham Competency Framework**
---------------------------------------------

At Mass General Brigham, our competency framework defines what effective leadership “looks like” by specifying which behaviors are most critical for successful performance at each job level. The framework is comprised of ten competencies (half People-Focused, half Performance-Focused) and are defined by observable and measurable skills and behaviors that contribute to workplace effectiveness and career success. These competencies are used to evaluate performance, make hiring decisions, identify development needs, mobilize employees across our system, and establish a strong talent pipeline.

new_roles.title: Sr. Manager Operations
new_roles.description:
**Job Description**

**Ingram Content Group (ICG)**is hiring a **Sr. Manager Operations** to support our **Distribution** team in **Jackson, TN**. The Sr. Manager, Operations manages the daily operations of an assigned area within the Distribution Center and serves as a key partner to the Director, Operations. This role collaborates with the Director on hiring, safety and security, maintenance and repairs, non-product purchasing, and strategic planning to ensure customer service levels and commitments are achieved, while maintaining a zero-error environment.

Want to join a key team that helps the world read?

At Ingram, the Operations team serves a key role within the organization. We ensure that our distribution centers and manufacturing facilities function at maximum efficiency. Safety is a core value in our operations environment. We emphasize this through training, education, and accident prevention programs. Process Improvement is another core value, and through innovations such as voice and Radio Frequency (RF) technologies, as well as feedback from our associates, we work toward constant improvement.

The world is reading, and it is our goal to connect as many people as possible to the content they want in the simplest ways. If you want to be part of a customer-centric team that strives for excellence, collaboration, innovation, we can’t wait to meet you!

**Schedule:**

* Monday-Friday, first shift, with flexibility to work weekends, additional hours, and provide on-call support as business needs require.

**What You’ll Need:**

* College degree OR HS diploma or GED with directly related year-for-year experience
* 6 years’ experience in a high-volume distribution center OR production/manufacturing facility with a clear track record of success
* 5 years’ experience supervising at least 25 or more employees

**What You’ll Do:**

* Achieve and maintain full working knowledge of all aspects of the assigned operation
* Implement a fast-paced, lean distribution system; drive the delivery of products and orders on time.
* Oversee KPIs, goals, and objectives for the management team; set clear goals and expectations for Managers and Area Managers, measure performance, provide feedback, and hold leaders accountable.
* Build a passionate team with a positive, inclusive, results-oriented culture; mentor and develop leaders and staff; manage staff selection and development, ensuring associates are fully trained and cross-trained on systems and procedures.
* Develop, manage, and lead continuous process improvement strategies and initiatives; leverage Lean, Six Sigma, and Performance Improvement tools to enhance productivity.
* Provide strategic-level/long-term planning (3, 6, and 12 months out), including labor planning, rate forecasting, and peak season planning.
* Work closely with support functions (HR, Maintenance/Engineering, Safety, IT, and other leaders) to build and secure support and resources for projects and initiatives.
* Ensure customer service levels exceed requirements and standards; works with management to improve cost-per-unit (CPU)/cost-per-line (CPL) while providing outstanding customer service.
* Collaborate with Senior Management in the planning, development, and launch of processes and strategies for the site; review competitive information and visit other companies to bring in new ideas on operations.
* Oversee the supervision of the operations area, ensuring the timely and accurate movement of materials into and out of the facility.
* Monitor and execute company policies and procedures for HR-related issues, including associate attendance, timekeeping, and performance reviews.
* Control and manage budget costs for all assigned departments/areas.

**Essential Physical Demands:**

* Ability to walk and stand as needed
* Ability to grip/grasp as needed
* Ability to lift/carry in full range of motion up to 60lbs as needed
* Ability to push/pull in a warehouse environment up to 70lbs force to push as needed
* Ability to bend, squat/kneel, twist/turn, climb, crawl, reach above shoulder, and type/keyboard frequently
* Ability to work a flexible which could include nights and weekends
* Ability to travel as needed
* Exposure to wide range of temperatures

*Hiring Salary Range: $113,201k - $143,945k. This range represents the anticipated low and high end of the salary for this position. It will be determined by factors including but not limited to: the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, geographic location, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.*

 **Additional Information**

**Perks/Benefits:**

* A highly competitive compensation package with generous benefits beginning first day of employment for Medical/Prescription Drug plans, HSA, Vision, Dental and Health Care FSA.
 + 15 vacation days & 12 sick days accrued annually and 3 personal days
 + 401K match, Life and AD&D, Employee Assistant programs, Group Legal, & more
* Encouraged continued education with our tuition reimbursement program
* Financial and in-kind opportunities to engage with non-profits in your community
 + Company match program for United Way donations
 + Volunteer opportunities and in-kind drives for non-profits throughout the year
* Casual Dress Code

The world is reading, and Ingram Content Group (“Ingram”) connects people with content in all forms. Providing comprehensive services for publishers, retailers, libraries and educators, Ingram makes these services seamless and accessible through technology, innovation and creativity. With an expansive global network of offices and facilities, Ingram’s services include digital and physical book distribution, print-on-demand, and digital learning. Ingram Content Group is a part of Ingram Industries Inc. and includes Ingram Book Group LLC, Ingram Publisher Services LLC, Lightning Source LLC, Ingram Library Services LLC, Tennessee Book Company LLC, Ingram Content Group UK Ltd. and Ingram Content Group Australia Pty Ltd.

new_roles.title: Regional Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
Circle of Life is growing, and we have an opening for a Regional Director of Operations to join our team. This position will oversee and manage our New Mexico branches; Albuquerque, Gallup, Kirtland, Shiprock, and Zuni.

**Good for employees**

Circle of Life’s focus is creating a workplace where respect, appreciation and teamwork are the shared experiences of our team. We do good for our employees by collaborating on scheduling, a focus on wellbeing, a client-first directive, respecting and valuing every team member, having fun along with top industry compensation and benefits.

**Good deeds**

We also do good in our work. Our team of office and field staff care about each other and the clients we serve. We help one another. We care and provide for a wide range of patients with a focus on serving the underserved.

**Position duties include**

* Participate in the hiring and training of managers
* Organize and oversee the work and schedules of managers
* Conduct performance evaluations
* Handle discipline of employees as needed following company policy
* Establish quantitative and qualitative metrics, guidelines, and standards by which the company's efficiency and effectiveness can be evaluated (identify opportunities for improvement)
* Implement policies and procedures that will improve day-to-day operations
* Oversee office operations, ensuring each branch is reaching goals set by departmental and company leadership
* Monitors budget and revenue in each office to achieve financial objectives
* Communicates and explains new directives, policies/procedures to manager for change and meets with staff to explain changes, answer questions, and maintain morale
* Improve customer service and satisfaction
* Market current products to potential clients, families, case workers and potential referral sources
* Leads coordination and integration of efforts among homecare teams to produce smoother workflow and more cost-effective business processes
* Traveling is required

**Qualifications**

Qualified applicants will have 3 years of management experience, excellent verbal and written communication skills and interpersonal and customer service skills. Healthcare and/or home care experience preferred. The Regional Director of Operations oversees the day-to-day activities for their assigned branches, ensuring the organization is managed and performing efficiently and effectively. While carrying out the responsibilities of the position, ensure the values of servant-leadership, empathy, altruism, and integrity are evident in all actions and encounters.

**How good?**

* Positively change the lives of individuals and families in our communities
* Serve the underserved providing access to care for those who have been traditionally overlooked by the health care system
* Support a talented team of administrative and clinical professionals and be a part of a team that supports each other

**Full Benefits include**

* Medical, Dental, 401K, Paid Holidays, Top PTO Plan, Mileage, Flexible Schedules, Vision, Year-End Bonus

Your impact: By strengthening care operations and performance improvement, you help patients and families receive coordinated, dependable homecare.

The ideal candidate will have strong adminstrative and communication skills, understand the importance of dependable home care services, and feel comfortable building relationships with healthcare professionals, social workers, case managers, and community organizations.

As a Home Director Of Operations, you’ll help clients access organized, responsive care by coordinating communication, records, and administrative support. You’ll manage client information with care, assist with scheduling and inquiries, and help ensure documentation follows applicable health regulations and privacy requirements. Your impact: By keeping care details accurate and communication clear, you help clients and care teams stay informed and better prepared for each step of service.
